claim_verdicts.evidence: seed.sql at stage-0: order_items for order 1 are ( 1, 1, 1, 1250000), ( 1, 2, 2, 450000) = 1250000 + 900000 = 2150000. WrongTotal.cs loops `for (var i = 0; i < lines.Count - 1; i++)` over `{ (1, 1_250_000), (2, 450_000) }`, so it sums the first line only and returns 1250000. The run confirms: `expected 2150000, got 1250000`.

Ran `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- wrong-total` from examples/don-hang. Full output, two lines: `expected 2150000, got 1250000` then `one line only: expected 1250000, got 0`. Program.cs at stage-0 maps ["wrong-total"] = Sync(WrongTotal.Run), so the sample name in the lesson is the one the dispatcher accepts.
claim_verdicts.source: execution in examples/don-hang; samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs at stage-0

The stage-0 page supports only the weaker statement: "Trợ lý sinh ra văn bản nghe hợp lý, không phải sự thật đã kiểm chứng." claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A plausible answer about a default carries no sign of having been checked, so an invented one can be worded just as confidently as a correct one; the wording alone is not a reliable way to tell them apart, and the official page for your version is.

claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-0:docs/craft/ai-prompt-examples.md` returns a Vietnamese page whose H2 headings are, in order, line 3 "## Câu hỏi tệ", line 11 "## Câu hỏi tốt", line 19 "## Ba việc nên giao", line 27 "## Ba việc không nên giao", line 34 "## Một câu để nhớ". Order and count match the lesson's description.

Lines 5-9 at stage-0: "> Viết cho tôi chức năng hủy đơn hàng." then "Không có phiên bản, không có ngữ cảnh, không có ràng buộc. Bạn sẽ nhận về một đoạn code trông hợp lý, dùng thư viện bạn không có, theo quy ước không phải của đội, và bạn không đủ thông tin để biết nó sai chỗ nào." One sentence, then the three costs as the lesson states them.

Lines 13-17 at stage-0 carry all five: "Đây là `OrderService.Cancel` của tôi (dán code)"; "Dự án dùng .NET 10 và PostgreSQL 17"; "chỉ đơn ở trạng thái `new` mới hủy được"; "Hiện tại đơn `shipped` cũng bị hủy"; "Đừng viết lại cả phương thức." It also asks "giải thích vì sao, và nói rõ điều gì trong .NET khiến nó xảy ra".

content/versions.yaml pins runtimes.dotnet.version "10.0" (lang "C# 14") and data.postgresql.version "17". The page's ".NET 10 và PostgreSQL 17" therefore names the pinned versions, and no other version appears anywhere in the lesson.

Lines 21-25 at stage-0 list exactly three numbered items: "**Giải thích code lạ.**" (checkable "bằng cách chạy thử"), "**Sinh test.** "Liệt kê các trường hợp biên cho phương thức này." Danh sách sai vẫn có ích; bạn chỉ cần đọc và loại bớt.", and "**Vịt cao su.** Viết vấn đề ra cho máy đọc, nhiều khi bạn tự thấy lỗi."

Lines 29-32 at stage-0 list exactly three: "**Câu hỏi về giá trị mặc định, giới hạn, phiên bản.** Hỏi tài liệu chính thức."; "**Code bạn không đọc từng dòng.** Bạn ký tên vào commit, không phải nó."; "**Dữ liệu thật của khách hàng.** Không dán vào bất kỳ công cụ ngoài nào."

Line 30 at stage-0 reads "Trợ lý sinh ra văn bản nghe hợp lý, không phải sự thật đã kiểm chứng." — the page's stated reason for sending default, limit and version questions to the official documentation, exactly as the lesson reports it.

Lines 36-38 at stage-0: "Trợ lý AI giống một đồng nghiệp rất tự tin, biết rất rộng, và thỉnh thoảng sai hoàn toàn mà giọng vẫn y hệt lúc đúng. Bạn đối xử với nó như với bản nháp của đồng nghiệp đó: đọc, kiểm tra, rồi mới dùng." The lesson keeps all three traits and the read-check-then-use order.

Line 31 at stage-0 reads "**Code bạn không đọc từng dòng.** Bạn ký tên vào commit, không phải nó." The lesson's sentence "Code you have not read line by line still enters a commit carrying your name, not the assistant's" is that sentence and no stronger.

The page supplies the contrast: its bad question is a line of intent, and its own stated cost is "bạn không đủ thông tin để biết nó sai chỗ nào"; its good question (lines 13-17) carries code, versions, rule, current wrong behaviour and one constraint. The "five parts" label is the lesson's own naming of those elements and the lesson does not attribute the label to the page.

The first half (a bare "still wrong" adds no information about the failure) is sound. The consequence "the next version is another guess" is a prediction about assistant behaviour with no source: versions.yaml pins no AI-assistant documentation, refs/ has none, and the stage-0 page says nothing about follow-up turns. The earlier turns stay in the exchange, so the outcome is likely, not certain.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A reply of "still wrong" carries no new information about the failure, so it gives the assistant nothing new to work from and the next version is likely to be another guess; the step that helps is a changed prompt.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Definitional: an answer that states its reasoning and names a page can be checked against that reasoning and that page, while one that states no basis offers nothing to check but itself. The half that could need a source has one — the page's good question asks "Chỉ ra chỗ sai, giải thích vì sao" (lines 16-17).

The page gives the cheap-check reason for two of its three itself: "bạn kiểm tra được câu trả lời bằng cách chạy thử" (explaining code) and "Danh sách sai vẫn có ích; bạn chỉ cần đọc và loại bớt" (test cases). The lesson's addition is marked as its own — "The page stops at three, but repetitive code that a single run can check belongs on the same side" — and is the boilerplate item of outline line 3.

Line 25 at stage-0: "**Vịt cao su.** Viết vấn đề ra cho máy đọc, nhiều khi bạn tự thấy lỗi." — write the problem out for a machine to read, and you often see the fault yourself. The lesson's "the third pays before it is answered" is that sentence, and the lesson attributes it to this item.

Lines 36-37 at stage-0: "thỉnh thoảng sai hoàn toàn mà giọng vẫn y hệt lúc đúng" — sometimes completely wrong in the very voice used when right. That is the claim: the voice does not separate a checked answer from an unchecked one, so an equally certain third version is the symptom, not a signal.

The commit half is on the page: "Bạn ký tên vào commit, không phải nó" (line 31). The clause "because someone on the team reads the change before it is merged" is not — the page says nothing about review, and review before merge is a team policy, not a fact about every team. The claim does not need it: the lesson's own second half (the code is later read and changed by people who ask why) already carries the responsibility point.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The person named on a commit answers for every line in it, whatever produced them: on teams that review before merge someone reads the change and asks why each line is there, and the code is later read and changed by people who ask why it is written that way.

claim_verdicts.evidence: This describes the lesson's own invented scenario in section 2, not the world: it says what the answer in that story showed, and nothing in it is offered as a general rule about assistants. Checked that section 4 does not turn it into one — it says only "Nothing in it said which project it was for, and what came back showed that". Nothing to source.

Line 5 at stage-0 is the single sentence "> Viết cho tôi chức năng hủy đơn hàng." — a request for an order-cancel feature, one line of intent with nothing attached, and a different subject from the wrong-total failure of section 2. Same shape, different subject, as the lesson states.

The page's term is "trường hợp biên" (boundary cases, line 22), which the gloss fits. The English label does not: refs/dotnet-docs .../unit-testing-mstest-writing-tests-data-driven.md:629 treats them as two things — "Choose test data that exercises edge cases and boundary conditions" — and unit-testing-best-practices.md:48 uses "edge cases" for untested conditional branches, not boundary inputs.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A boundary case is an input at the edge of what a method accepts.

claim_verdicts.evidence: The page states the rule with no reason — "**Dữ liệu thật của khách hàng.** Không dán vào bất kỳ công cụ ngoài nào" (line 32) — while its other two kept-back items do carry the reasons the claim names (lines 30 and 31). The lesson supplies the disclosure reason in its own voice ("here the risk is disclosure, not a wrong answer") and does not put it in the page's mouth.

This is the definition of a unit test, not of a test. refs/dotnet-docs/docs/core/testing/index.md: "A *unit test* is a test that exercises individual software components or methods"; the same section defines an integration test ("exercises two or more software components' ability to function together") and a load test, neither of which calls one method on chosen inputs. Naming the kind costs one word.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A unit test is a small run that calls a method on chosen inputs and checks what comes back.

issues.quote: an invented one is worded exactly like a correct one. Nothing in the wording separates them
issues.text: Absolute as written, and nothing pinned supports it: versions.yaml names no AI-assistant documentation and the stage-0 page claims only "văn bản nghe hợp lý, không phải sự thật đã kiểm chứng". Invented answers about defaults often do carry signs — an option name that does not exist, an example that contradicts the stated default. The lesson needs only the weaker form, and summary line 2 repeats the same absolute: "an invented answer is written exactly like a correct one".
issues.fix: Section 4: "an invented one can be worded just as confidently as a correct one. The wording alone is not a reliable way to separate them; the official page for your version is." Make summary line 2 match ("can be written just like a correct one"). Then reword q2 option a from "Nothing that tells the two apart" to "Nothing they can rely on to tell the two apart" so the key stays the only defensible option.

issues.quote: a reply that carries no new information gives the assistant nothing new to work from, so the next version is another guess
issues.text: The consequence is stated as certain. It is a prediction about assistant behaviour with no source available (no AI-assistant key in versions.yaml, nothing in refs/, nothing on the stage-0 page about follow-up turns), and it is not always true: the earlier turns stay in the exchange, so a bare "still wrong" sometimes does produce a corrected version.
issues.fix: Write "so the next version is likely to be another guess", or stop at the defensible half: "a reply that carries no new information gives the assistant nothing new to work from." Update claim 14 in .meta.json to the wording you keep.

issues.quote: someone on your team reads the change before it is merged and asks why each line is there
issues.text: Stated as a fact about every team. Review before merge is a team policy; the stage-0 page says only "Bạn ký tên vào commit, không phải nó" and nothing about review. The responsibility point does not need the universal — the lesson's own next clause (the code will be read, changed and broken by people who ask why it is written this way) already carries it.
issues.fix: Condition it: "on teams that review before merge, someone reads the change and asks why each line is there". Section 6's misconception answer and q6 option c ("to whoever reads the change before it is merged") already read as conditional and need no change. Update claim 19 in .meta.json.

issues.quote: generating tests — small runs that call a method on chosen inputs and check what comes back
issues.text: That defines a unit test, not a test. The pinned .NET documentation (refs/dotnet-docs/docs/core/testing/index.md) defines a unit test as "a test that exercises individual software components or methods" and in the same section defines integration and load tests, which do not call one method on chosen inputs. A junior who takes this as the definition of "test" is wrong the first time someone says integration test.
issues.fix: Insert one word: "generating unit tests — small runs that call a method on chosen inputs and check what comes back". Update claim 24 in .meta.json to the same wording.

issues.quote: edge cases (the unusual inputs at the boundaries of what it accepts)
issues.text: The gloss describes boundary cases, which is what the quoted page asks for ("Liệt kê các trường hợp biên cho phương thức này"), but the English term chosen is wider: refs/dotnet-docs .../unit-testing-mstest-writing-tests-data-driven.md:629 lists "edge cases and boundary conditions" as two things, and unit-testing-best-practices.md:48 uses "edge cases" for untested conditional branches.
issues.fix: Use "boundary cases (inputs at the edges of what the method accepts)" in section 5; it also translates "trường hợp biên" in the block you quote. Update claim 22 in .meta.json.

issues.quote: an answer you cannot judge saves no work
issues.text: Absolute, and not in the claims ledger — the nearest entry, claim 13, is about a prompt that yields a judgeable answer, not about the worth of an unjudgeable one. It is also not quite true: an answer you cannot judge can still name an API or a direction you then look up yourself, which is work saved.
issues.fix: Write "an answer you cannot judge saves less than it looks like it saves", or cut the sentence and let the page's own "bạn không đủ thông tin để biết nó sai chỗ nào" carry the point. If kept in any form, add it to the claims in .meta.json.
